title: Marvel vs. Capcom 2, and VS.COM
body: From the Japanese disc: the title screen, now the right way round (a light logo on a dark screen; the old screenshot had it inverted), the ACCESS screen, and VS.COM, the VMU program the game copies to the memory card, with its Capcom logo, title, menu, copyright, shop and trade screens in Japanese and English. Its fonts, character names, ranks and menu parts are in the Sprites card. Three more save icons the game writes, UPLOAD, DOWNLOAD and Capcom network, come straight from the disc, which also confirms the two already here.

title: Game pages in tabs
body: A game's screens, sprites, fonts and notes are now tabs at the top of its page, so you can go straight to the sprites without scrolling past every screen. Press 1 to 4 to switch, and a link keeps the tab you're on. A game's save icons now sit beside its title.

title: Save icons
body: A new page for the colour icons the Dreamcast's memory card menu shows for each save, every game's in one grid you can search: 520 icons from 344 games, read from a collection of dumped saves, each kept once however many saves carry it, with the name the game gave the save on the memory card. Some memory cards' own icons are there too, colour and VMU side by side, marked unverified until a game's disc shows it made them; and the VMU mini-games that came with games, like Chao Adventure and Pinta's Quest.

title: Jet Set Radio, and its graffiti viewer
body: Twelve screens from the Japanese disc: the katakana logo, the radio turning on its loop, Now Saving, Now Loading, OK and NG, and the graffiti viewer the game copies to the VMU, with its SEGA and copyright screens, title, menus and blinking Press A. Its fonts and radio parts are in the Sprites card.

title: Sprites, out from behind the scenes
body: The smaller art games draw onto part of a screen, like digits, buttons, fonts and faces, now has its own Sprites card on each game's page: all 341 of Shenmue's, the Dreamcast BIOS's 129 memory card icons, Power Stone Mini's, the VMU's fonts and clock animals, Ikaruga's chain digits and Sakura Taisen 3's battle parts. Hover one for its name.

title: Falcon's course, scrolling down
body: Screens can now scroll down as well as sideways. The first is the course of Power Stone Mini's Falcon game: one whole lap, frame for frame as the game draws it, moving at Falcon's cruising speed. That speed comes from the code, but the length of a tick is still an estimate.

title: Power Stone Mini
body: The VMU game hidden in Power Stone's program: its title, the Capcom and copyright screens, both of Falcon, Ayame and Gunrock's portraits, and the Japanese rules, slot prompts, high scores and rewards of Falcon's Aerial Adventure, Ayame's Shuriken Training and Gun-Gun Slots. Its sprites, reels and the whole Falcon course are kept too.

title: The Shenmue Goodies viewer
body: From Shenmue's Passport disc, the VMU program that showed the Goodies: its あつめて シェンムー title, a Dreamcast logo and a brush-stroke drawing. It also holds the four characters it comes with, which match the ones already here pixel for pixel.

title: Shenmue's Goodies characters
body: 213 Shenmue characters animated on the VMU, from Ryo and Lan Di to the neighbourhood cats, the Goodies that Shenmue Passport's online service traded for Winning Cans until 2002. They come from the Neoseeker Shenmue wiki, with the four built-in characters' portraits. Ryo Hazuki now plays the wiki's version. Their timing is the wiki's and hasn't been checked against the game.

title: Shenmue, straight from the disc
body: Shenmue's own VMU screens from the Japanese disc: the 莎木 title logo, the start, count and cleared screens of the 70 Man Battle, and its English Please Wait. Its loading, saving, OK, NG and PK screens are the same pictures Shenmue II uses, so they stay filed there.

title: The VMU's own main menu
body: The screen the Visual Memory Unit shows by itself, with no game: the SEGA logo over "Visual Memory Unit", drawn by the US VMU BIOS every time it returns to its menu. Read from a commented disassembly of that BIOS, which also gave up the dog, fish and bird of its clock animation and both of its fonts, kept behind the scenes with the Dreamcast BIOS's 129 memory card icons.

title: Shinseiki Evangelion: Typing E-Keikaku
body: Every VMU screen in Gainax's Evangelion typing game: its title logo, and the Access, Save OK, Save NG, Load OK and Load NG screens it shows while saving and loading. The first Windows CE game in the archive. Nothing on its VMU animates.

title: Crazy Taxi 2
body: Every VMU screen in the US Crazy Taxi 2: its title screen, flames dancing over the logo, and the Now Loading and Now Saving screens. The title plays at 267 ms a frame, which assumes the game runs at 60 Hz, until a capture confirms it.

title: The rest of Ikaruga
body: Every other VMU screen from the Japanese Ikaruga disc: the blinking Save screen, Load, OK and NG, and the chain counter, drawn from a set of digits over a CHAIN panel. Also a second Load screen, with the bird in another pose, that the game never shows. The Save blink's speed is read from the game's code and not yet measured.

title: Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in the Japanese Street Fighter III 3rd Strike: the title screen, and the Access, OK and Error screens it shows while saving and loading. Nothing on its VMU animates.

title: Browse by game
body: The archive now opens on a grid of its games, searchable by their English or Japanese titles. Each game has its own page with its screens, a search within them, and notes on how they were extracted from the disc. Old links still work.

title: The rest of Sakura Taisen 3
body: Everything else on the Sakura Taisen 3 disc: the power-on animation, the logo intros of the three Kajino Taisen minigames, the second crest and the strategy map, and the faces now blink. Their timing is a best guess until it's measured.

title: Soul Calibur's fighters
body: All 19 fighters from Soul Calibur, the little figures the game shows on the VMU, five poses each, decompressed from the US disc with the game's own routine. They play at the site's default speed until their in-game timing is measured.

title: Sakura Taisen 3, with scrolling banners
body: From the Japanese Sakura Taisen 3 disc: the title screen with its logo intro, the crest, and four expressions each for Erica, Glycine, Coquelicot, Lobelia, Hanabi and Ogami. Also the 23 special attack banners the game scrolls across the VMU in battle, stored as the one strip the game slides through the screen and played at its speed. They download as that strip, or as an animation.

title: Shenmue II, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in the Japanese Shenmue II: the title screen, loading, saving and resume screens in Japanese and English, and the battle screens.

title: Power Stone and Power Stone 2, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in both games: the Access screens for Power Stone and Power Stone 2, and the Power Stone 2 title screen. The Power Stone title screen already in the archive matches the disc exactly.

title: Project Justice, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in the Japanese Moero! Justice Gakuen: the Japanese title screen, and the Access screen under both the Japanese and Project Justice logos.

title: Bangaioh, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in the Japanese Bakuretsu Muteki Bangaioh, played with the timing from the game's own code: the Japanese title screen and the Riki and Mami loops. Four more the game never shows are marked Unused: the Treasure logo, a second Riki and Mami loop each, and an animated Continue?.

title: Berserk, straight from the disc
body: Every Puck screen, extracted from the Sword of the Berserk disc and played with the timing read from the game's own code: seven new animations, the NG screen, the US title screen, and Do not touch now animated in full. Six screens the game never shows are marked Unused.

title: Bangai-O
body: The title screen from Treasure's shooter Bangai-O, and its animated robot.

title: Ryo Hazuki comes to life
body: Shenmue's Ryo Hazuki is now animated. You can also pick a game next to the search box to see only its screens.

title: Carrier
body: The title screen from Jaleco's survival horror Carrier.

title: Sega Tetris
body: The title screen, the memory card screens and the full cast of animated characters, from Bowie to Panna-Panna.

title: Title screens and the first animations
body: Title screens from Blue Stinger, Legacy of Kain: Soul Reaver, Marvel vs. Capcom 2, Power Stone, Rez and Shenmue, the Dreamcast menu smile and screens from Berserk, including Puck. Animated screens now play on hover and download as GIF or animated SVG. The Crazy Taxi title screen is animated too.

title: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater
body: All 35 screens: the title screen, loading and saving, and every reaction from "Rad" to "U suck".

title: The archive opens
body: The first 128 screens: the whole Puyo Pop Fever cast, Sonic Adventure and Sonic Adventure 2, and title screens from Crazy Taxi, Ikaruga, Jet Set Radio, Project Justice, Sonic Shuffle and Soul Calibur.
